 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 26-07-2024 at about 1-00 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA- 01/MX-0560 from Gannikada to Channarayapatna and when they reached near Gannikada Bridge, he parked his Car on the extreme left side of the road and stood to view the river, at that time Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/W-7571 came from Holenarasipura in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Grass life Hospital,
Channarayapatna wherein taken treatment.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical and conveyance expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he has aged about 50 years.
The petitioner was Agriculturist by profession and also doing business of his own and earning Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. The Respondent no.1/RC owner of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/W-7571 filed written statement and contended that the accident in question was due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.

5. The Respondent no.2/insurer of Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/W-7571 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the rider of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence and careless act on the part of the petitioner in driving the car Jagadeesha K L vs Prakasha M N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163804883/
2 bearing No.KA-01-MX- 0560 and stopped the car in the middle of the road to see the river view and opened the door all of a sudden without seeing the vehicular movement in the said road result of which the petitioner sustained minor injures and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle.

sentences.text:
6. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
7.

Based on the pleadings, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 26-07-2024 at about 1.00 p.m., on Gannikada Bridge, Kasaba Hobli, at Holenarasipura Taluk, Hassan, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-13-W-7571?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What order or Award ?
8.
The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the rider of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 26-07-2024 at about 1-00 p.m., when the petitioner was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-01/MX-0560 from Gannikada to Channarayapatna and when he reached near Gannikada Bridge, he parked his Car on the extreme left side of the road and stood to view the river,
at that time Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13/W-7571 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) came from Holenarasipura in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R. with Complaint, Victim statement, Crime details form, Seizure mahazar with photos, IMV report, Charge sheet, Wound certificate etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri.Mahesh .K.R, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.102/2024 by Holenarasipura Rural Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a) and 281 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

After completion of investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 281, 125(a) and 125(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sec 146 and 196 of IMV Act.
13. It is relevant to state here that at the inception, the petition was filed against the respondent no.1 and 2 alone.

Later on, as per the application filed by the respondent no.2, the respondent no.3 was arrayed and respondent no.3 filed written statement, wherein contended that the policy issued by them in respect of the alleged offending vehicle does not cover the risk as on the date of accident and filed necessary application to delete them from the proceedings.
The said application was allowed and as per the order dated 01-07-2025 the respondent no.3 was deleted from the proceedings.

14. The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the rash and negligence contributed by the rider of the offending vehicle and strenuously contended that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner who parked his car in the middle of the road.

15. In the light of the contention taken by the respondent no.2, if the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 24 feet and the said road runs North to South direction.
There is 4 feet footpath on either side of the road and the accident in question has occurred at a distance of nearly 6 feet from the Western side of the road.
As per the own case of the petitioner, they have parked their vehicle at the end of the bridge so as to view the river.
There is preventive wall ( ) on both sides of the bridge.

When there is footpath of the width of 4 feet on both sides of the road adjoining to preventive wall, the petitioner could have viewed the river by standing in the footpath and there was no necessity for them to stand in the tar road that too at a distance of nearly 6 feet from the left edge of the footpath towards right side.
Hence, it can be said without any hesitation that the petitioner too has contributed negligence.
Further, when it is nowhere the case of respondent no.2 and it is nowhere stated in the spot mahazar and sketch that there is curve near the spot of accident.

When it can be made out that the said road is a straight road, under such circumstances if the rider of the offending vehicle had driven his vehicle in moderate speed, on seeing the petitioner standing in the road, he could have avoided the accident by applying break or by taking his vehicle on the right side of the road.
Hence, the rider of the offending vehicle has contributed higher amount of negligence.
Hence, the negligence contributed by the petitioner is assessed at 15% and the negligence contributed by the rider of the offending vehicle is assessed at 85%.
The petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 15% negligence contributed by him.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.

As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge Jagadeesha K L vs Prakasha M N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163804883/
4 summary which are marked at Ex.P7 and P8.

sentences.text: On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment at Grass Life hospital, Channarayapatna from 26-07-2024 to 29-07-2021 for a period of 4 days
As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is grievous in nature and injury no.2 is simple in nature.
17. Mohan A S - Incharge Administration, Grass Life Hospital at Channarayapattna is examined as PW.2 and through him Case sheet and x-ray films are got marked as Ex.P12 and Ex.P13.

18. Dr. S. Ramachandra - Senior Consultant in Orthopaedics and DNB Post Graduates Professor at General Hosptial, Bengaluru is examined as Pw.3 and through him OPD Card and X-ray film are got marked as Ex.P14 and 15.
P.W.3 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 21-07-2025 for assessment of disability.

PW.3 further deposed that the petitioner suffered permanent residual physical disability of left lower limb at 34.50% and to the whole body at 17.25% and that the petitioner need one more surgery for removal of implant from Tibia and Fibula of left leg.
19. If the evidence of PW.3 is perused, he is not a treated doctor.
As per the own evidence of Pw.3 the fracture is united and he has no information regarding the avocation of the petitioner.
It is nowhere stated by the PW.3 that due to the injuries and the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner cannot continue his work.
As per the case of petitioner, he is a business man and agriculturist.

The learned counsel for petitioner has vehemently submitted by referring three judgments that the petitioner is to be awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- each towards pain and sufferings and loss of amenities and the percentage of disability assessed by the PW.3 has to be considered while computing the future loss of income.
20.
In the judgment referred by the learned counsel in Civil Appeal No. 9205/2013 (Arising out of SLP (c) No.24419/2011) between Mohammed Saleem Vs. Regl. Manager National Ins.Ltd., & Anr.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There was shorting of right lower limb of the claimant apart from other severe injuries suffered by him.
The doctor has opined that the claimant has permanent disability of 30% on right lower limb and 15% on whole body.

In the said case, reference was made of case in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and observed that "when disability certificate states that the injured has suffered permanent disability to certain percentage with reference to particular limb it is not the same percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body.
In the said case, the doctor has given evidence that due to the accident the claimant is not able to do his earlier work or any other manual work.
In the said case, the claimant has taken treatment for a period 46 days.

In the given set of facts the Hon'ble Supreme Court has considered the percentage of disability on whole body assessed by the doctor and awarded Rs.1,00,000/- as loss of amenities and prospects of marriage and sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of expectation of life and Rs.1,00,000/ towards loss of earning during the period of treatment and future loss of income.
21.

In Civil Appeal No.8074/2024 (SC) ..between Suresh Vs. Senthil B & Anr., In the said case,
injured was weaver.
The medical expert has assessed the disability of 64% on the right lower limb and 32% disability with respect to whole body.
The doctor has opined that the claimant being employed as a weaver, as a consequence of the injuries sustained in the accident is unable to do his work.

Hence, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has considered 32% of disability one assessed by the Jagadeesha K L vs Prakasha M N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163804883/
5 medical expert to asses the future loss of income.

sentences.text: 22. Coming to the case in hand, the petitioner has taken treatment only for 4 days.
Further he is married hence the question of awarding compensation for loss of prospect of marriage does not arise.
Further PW.3 nowhere has stated that petitioner cannot to do any work because of the disability suffered by him.
Pw.3 having assessed the disability on left lower limb at 34.50% assessed the disability on whole body at 17.25%.

But in the judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk it was observed that "normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3 rd of the particular limb".

entities.text: 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this court inclines to assess the disability of petitioner on whole body at 12%.
23. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
24. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous and one simple injury.

Hence taking in to consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
25. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced one inpatient final discharge bill for Rs.80,000/- as per Ex.P10.
The respondent has not much disputed the genuineness of the bill.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 80,000/-.
26.
It is stated that petitioner was doing Real Estate Business and Agriculture and was earning a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- per month.
To substantiate the said contention the petitioner has not produced any materials.

In the absence of such document, this Tribunal considering the age of the petitioner, year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
27.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous and one simple injury and taken treatment at Grass life hospital, Channarayapatna.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner which is grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 5 months as complete laid down period.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.82,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
28. From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Grass life hospital, Channarayapatna.

Further for 4 days of hospitalization requires an attendant,
was traveled to hospital for treatment, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of money during the year 2024.

6 29.

sentences.text: The petitioner has contended that he is aged about 50 years as on the date of accident.
Petitioner has produced his Aadhar card which is marked as Ex.P9, which shows his date of birth as 02.05.1974 that means he was aged about 50 years.
Hence considering the Aadhar Card this court has taken the age of the petitioner as 50 years at the time of accident.

30. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.16,500/- p.m and by considering the evidence of PW.3 though he has assessed disability at 17.25%, but this court inclines to take the disability on whole body at 12% and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 50 years, as per Sarla Varma's case, the multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is '13'.
So by applying the multiplier '13' the future loss of income due to disability would comes to Rs.3,08,880/- (i.e., 16,500 x 12% x 13 x 12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,08,880/- towards future loss of income due to disability.

31. So far as future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.3 has deposed that the petitioner is advised to undergo another operation for removal of implants from Tibia and Fibula of left leg,
but he has not given any estimation.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- towards Future medical expenses.
32. The petitioner at his age of 50 years has suffered one grievous and one simple injury.
Hence it may cause some amount of loss of amenities and discomfort.
Hence this court inclines to award sum of Rs.50,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 70,000-00 2.
Medical expenses Rs. 80,000-00 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 82,500-00  laid up period
4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000-00  charges and nourishing food 5. Loss of Future Income Rs. 3,08,880-00 6.
Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000-00 7. loss of comfort and amenities Rs. 50,000-00

Total Rs. 6,46,380-00 Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.6,46,380/- (Rupees Six Lakh Forty Six Thousand Three Hundred Eighty only).
33.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 15:85 this court has Jagadeesha K L vs Prakasha M N on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163804883/
7 already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 15%.

sentences.text: The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 85% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
85% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
34. Issue No.3: In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.6,46,380/- (Rupees Six Lakh Forty Six Thousand Three Hundred Eighty only).

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 85% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.5,49,423/- +
cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on IA No. I, in all sum of Rs.5,49,923/- (Rupees Five Lakh Forty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Twenty Three only) with interest on sum of Rs.5,19,423/- at 6% pa., within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.5,19,423/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 15% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.96,957/-.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 60% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 40% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
